pregnancy.266: If you haven't found out the sex of your baby, the excitement will be building; if you have, you can get very organized!
pregnancy.267: With labor imminent, you'll be playing the waiting game. Staying active will help the time pass much more quickly.
pregnancy.268: Although your baby will be born with beautifully big eyes, it will be some time before he will see clearly at a distance.
pregnancy.269: If you're having a home birth, you can make the midwife's task as easy as possible by being well organized.
pregnancy.270: Could your baby be dreaming already? A lot of his movements are occurring when he's fast asleep.
pregnancy.271: Don't just wait for contractions - it's worth familiarizing yourself now with the signs that may mean labor is imminent.
pregnancy.272: Because you're heading into the final week, you're bound to feel a little anxious, but hopefully excited, too.
pregnancy.273: Use this time in the lead-in to labor to get your partner fully up to speed on how he can help you on the big day.
pregnancy.274: It's good to revisit your birth plan at this late stage since you may feel differently now about some of the requests you made.
pregnancy.275: Your baby's bones have hardened to a certain degree, but this process will continue right up to the teenage years!
pregnancy.276: The inquiries may begin flooding in this week and it will feel as though the whole world is awaiting news of your baby's arrival.
pregnancy.277: Don't be too concerned if your baby hasn't engaged yet since this won't have any bearing on the final delivery date.
pregnancy.278: You'll be in labor very soon and it's normal to be anxious about what you need to go through to meet your baby.
pregnancy.279: Your newborn's stomach will be fully developed, but low acid levels mean she can only be fed milk for the first few months.
pregnancy.280: You've reached 40 weeks exactly! It may have seemed like a long wait, but it will be worth it once you're holding your baby.
pregnancy.281: Most women do not go into labor at exactly 40 weeks and anything between 37 and 42 weeks is considered normal. Try to rest, relax and eat well during this time.
pregnancy.282: Although no "home" remedy has been proven to bring on labor, there are harmless techniques thought to assist the body’s natural process. Probably the most enjoyable way is to make love with your partner. Sperm contains prostaglandins that may act as a natural uterine stimulant.
pregnancy.283: Although no "home" remedy has been proven to bring on labor, you can also try stimulating your nipples. This can cause the release of oxytocin from your pituitary gland which is linked to contractions and cervical ripening.  Please do so only under the supervision of your healthcare provider.
pregnancy.284: Walking and exercise may cause a mild increase in uterine contractions by helping the baby move down the pelvis, putting pressure on the cervix.
pregnancy.285: Going over your due date can be stressful, but it may help to remind yourself that this quite common.  And most overdue babies have a normal birth weight.
pregnancy.286: For 22.3 percent of women in the US, labor is started by artificial means, or induced, to reduce the risk to you and your baby.
pregnancy.287: After 41 weeks, there is a slightly increase risk to your baby’s health that may be due to the reduced efficiency of the placenta. Your doctor or midwife will be monitoring the situation closely.
pregnancy.288: Studies have revealed a good 70% of pregnancies are not overdue at all; the reason for the delay is miscalculation at the time of conception. Miscalculation happens because of irregular ovulation or confusion over the exact date of the last menstrual period.
pregnancy.289: Prenatal care will continue after you pass your due date. Your healthcare provider will watch for signs of complications, such as preeclampsia. He or she will also check your cervix to see if it's begun to thin and dilate in preparation for labor.
pregnancy.290: Before an induction, you will have an internal examination to assess your cervix. Induction is easier if your cervix is short and soft.  This is described as having a favorable or ripe cervix.
pregnancy.291: If you cervix is not ripe by now, it can be softened with prostaglandins. These are naturally occurring chemicals that help stimulate contractions. Sometimes, this fails to work and may be tried again in a few days. On the other hand, you may experience dramatic effects after a small dose.
pregnancy.292: Your doctor may also elect to break your water. Breaking it can get your contractions started or make them stronger. Most women will go into labor hours of their water breaking. If labor does not begin, another method may be used to bring on contractions.
pregnancy.293: Your doctor can also give you a medicine called oxytocin. This medicine will make your uterus contract to begin the labor process. During labor, your doctor will take special precautions to make sure both you and the baby are safe.
pregnancy.294: Many doctors will induce labor at this point. If you do not want to be induced, your doctor may offer monitoring with scans to measure the baby’s pulse and volume of fluid around the baby.  You are not alone – nearly 7% of babies are born more than 2 weeks overdue.
pregnancy.295: If you and your doctor have chosen not to induce at this point, please work closely together to monitor the baby and to assess the risks to you and your baby.

postpartum.1: Finally, your baby is in your arms! As you recuperate in the hospital, you’ll get to know the baby you’ve waited to meet.
postpartum.2: You may be feeling anxious about your new responsibilities, but be reassured by the support network around you.
postpartum.3: Once your breast milk arrives, your baby may start to appear more relaxed and contented and go longer between feedings.
postpartum.4: Your body is gradually recovering from the birth, and you may be starting to feel like facing the world once again.
postpartum.5: Try to spend some time focusing on the needs of older children too and helping them to adapt to the new arrival.
postpartum.6: By now, you and your partner will be starting to feel more confident about holding, handling, and feeding your baby.
postpartum.7: As the bond between you and your baby continues to grow, you will start to feel more intuitive about his needs.
postpartum.8: A healthy lifestyle benefits your physical and mental well-being and helps you deal with the demands of parenthood.
postpartum.9: Now that you’ve begun to adapt to the topsy-turvy world of motherhood, try to carve out some time for yourself each day.
postpartum.10: If you find that you need some additional help with the baby, there are several options to consider.
postpartum.11: Part of becoming a parent is learning to trust your own instincts, even if this sometimes means ignoring the advice of others.
postpartum.12: For some, reliving a traumatic birth is painful and you and your partner may need support to work through difficult memories.
postpartum.13: Now that you and your partner are adapting to your new roles, you can start to think about how to make time for each other.
postpartum.14: Life will never be the same again and by now you will understand the unconditional love of a parent for their child.
